output.review_comment:
Three behavioral changes are bundled here: (1) sorting keys alphabetically instead of preserving insertion order, (2) lower-casing booleans to "true"/"false" instead of the default str() output, and (3) switching from quote_plus to quote so spaces become %20 instead of +. Each of these is a real behavior change, not just a bug fix in the existing logic — and the code comments read like they were reverse-engineered from what makes the tests pass ("Sort keys alphabetically to ensure consistent ordering", "Use quote instead of quote_plus to encode spaces as %20") rather than quoted/justified from the actual docstring text.

The diff doesn't show the full docstring (only the trailing line "If nothing is left to encode, the result is ""), so there's no way to confirm from this PR alone that sorting, boolean casing, and %20-vs-+ encoding are actually specified contracts rather than incidental choices that happen to satisfy the test suite. Since the whole premise of the task is "the docstring is the source of truth," the PR should make that traceability explicit — e.g. quote the relevant docstring sentences in the PR description and/or as inline comments referencing them, rather than comments that just describe what the code now does.

Also note the PR description is empty, which makes it harder to verify intent. Please add a description that maps each change back to the specific docstring language it's satisfying, so a reviewer without access to the full file can confirm this isn't just curve-fitting to the test suite. If the docstring does spell these out explicitly, this is likely fine to merge — but that needs to be shown, not assumed.
